title: Loan balance with early repayments
prompt:
A loan has an outstanding balance of $53947.92 at the start of month 1. The nominal annual interest rate is 7.80%, i.e. the monthly interest rate is 0.65%. Every month the following happens, in this order:
  1. interest = (balance at the start of the month) × (monthly rate in effect for that month), rounded to the nearest cent (half a cent rounds up);
  2. the interest is added to the balance and the regular payment of $445.00 is subtracted;
  3. if an extra prepayment is scheduled for that month, it is subtracted as well.
The balance after step 3 is the balance at the start of the next month. The regular payment stays $445.00 for the whole period. Scheduled events:
- At the end of month 3, after the regular payment, an extra prepayment of $1280.00 is made.
- At the end of month 8, after the regular payment, an extra prepayment of $2394.09 is made.
- At the end of month 10, after the regular payment, an extra prepayment of $215.00 is made.
- Starting with month 26, the monthly interest rate becomes 0.55% (annual 6.60%).
- Starting with month 27, the monthly interest rate becomes 0.50% (annual 6.00%).
- Starting with month 32, the monthly interest rate becomes 0.45% (annual 5.40%).
- Starting with month 36, the monthly interest rate becomes 0.40% (annual 4.80%).
- At the end of month 39, after the regular payment, an extra prepayment of $2137.00 is made.
- Starting with month 41, the monthly interest rate becomes 0.50% (annual 6.00%).
- At the end of month 57, after the regular payment, an extra prepayment of $1858.98 is made.
- At the end of month 70, after the regular payment, an extra prepayment of $722.00 is made.
- Starting with month 79, the monthly interest rate becomes 0.60% (annual 7.20%).
- Starting with month 81, the monthly interest rate becomes 0.75% (annual 9.00%).
- Starting with month 82, the monthly interest rate becomes 0.65% (annual 7.80%).

What is the outstanding balance at the end of month 84 (after all steps of month 84)? Give the amount in dollars with exactly two decimals, without the $ sign and without thousands separators (e.g. 12345.67).

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.

title: Sorting words by an invented alphabet
prompt:
An invented language uses only the following 12 letters, and its alphabetical order is (from first to last):

  b < n < z < o < i < p < t < u < e < r < k < d

Words are compared letter by letter from the left: at the first position where they differ, the word whose letter comes earlier in this alphabet comes first. (No word in the list is a beginning of another.)

Sort the following 79 words in increasing alphabetical order of this language:

kbozpuz, bozore, kndub, doneti, tzodu, kbi, tiu, kboez, kir, kndp, bubob, ziper, potib, ponib, kbozour, koi, boriru, zitin, tzopk, kboepzrr, nuritzi, ponetd, zizzui, kurii, kize, kbkor, rzrn, ponkbk, nuribeb, zipd, kboeood, porik, tzke, rubobuk, tedoi, potinp, poneb, dozu, kndudu, kbok, ribuz, teno, konikb, zitio, zin, rido, bunou, ponorbn, buzizuo, ponozi, kiden, kut, poneu, koe, zipnn, kotri, tio, kiori, rinbt, kod, kuniti, ponuzz, tekzud, bir, kokn, kuuzk, kop, tzkn, zipipt, rit, kbrer, zir, tenpdpe, kond, bopo, ribbbei, nee, potiz, bipi

title: Diffie–Hellman shared keys
prompt:
Alice and Bob run a textbook Diffie–Hellman key exchange with the public prime p = 701 and the public generator g = 3 (a primitive root modulo p). Alice picks a secret exponent a and publishes A = g^a mod p = 288; Bob picks a secret exponent b and publishes B = g^b mod p = 202 (1 ≤ a, b ≤ p − 2). The shared secret is K = g^(a·b) mod p = B^a mod p = A^b mod p.

Recover the shared secret K (you will need to find one of the secret exponents, e.g. by computing successive powers of g modulo p). Give K as an integer between 0 and p − 1.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.

title: Selection in a one-locus model
prompt:
A diploid population has one locus with two alleles, A and a. Genotype fitnesses (relative viabilities) are w(AA) = 0.70, w(Aa) = 0.80, w(aa) = 0.95. Generations are discrete and non-overlapping, mating is random (Hardy–Weinberg proportions among zygotes), there is no mutation, migration or drift. If p is the frequency of A in one generation, the frequency in the next generation is

  p' = (p²·w(AA) + p·q·w(Aa)) / (p²·w(AA) + 2·p·q·w(Aa) + q²·w(aa)),  where q = 1 − p.

The initial frequency is p₀ = 0.88. Rounding rule: after computing each generation, round p' to 4 decimal places (round half up) and use this rounded value for the next generation.

What is the frequency of A after 10 generations (p_10)? Give it rounded to 4 decimal places.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.
